t: This is HM Prison Brixton, a men's prison in Lambeth, run by His Majesty's Prison Service. It's a Category C training prison now, though before 2012 it served as a local prison. It matters in Irish history because of Terence MacSwiney, a playwright, author and politician who was elected Sinn Féin Lord Mayor of Cork in 1920, during the Irish War of Independence. Arrested by the British government on charges of sedition, he was imprisoned here. He died in October 1920 after seventy-four days on hunger strike, which brought him and the Irish Republican campaign international attention.
